what_its_for: This medicine helps lower your LDL cholesterol (the 'bad' cholesterol) in your blood. It is used along with a healthy diet to reduce your risk of heart disease, heart attacks, and stroke. It works in two ways: bempedoic acid blocks your liver from making too much cholesterol, and ezetimibe reduces how much cholesterol your body absorbs from food.
how_to_take: Swallow one tablet by mouth once a day. You can take it with or without food. Try to take it at the same time each day to help you remember. Do not crush, chew, or split the tablet — swallow it whole.
dosing: The usual dose is one tablet (180 mg bempedoic acid / 10 mg ezetimibe) taken once daily. Always follow the exact dose your doctor prescribed. Do not take more or less than directed.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it has been fewer than 12 hours since your scheduled dose. If more than 12 hours have passed, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store this medicine at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it in the original container with the cap tightly closed. Store it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Keep out of reach of children and pets. Do not store in the bathroom.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking more than the prescribed amount. Tell your doctor about all other medicines you take, especially cyclosporine, gemfibrozil, or other cholesterol-lowering medicines, as these may interact with this drug. Limit alcohol intake, as it can raise triglycerides and increase your risk of liver problems. Avoid making major changes to your diet without talking to your doctor or dietitian first.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: sudden or unexplained muscle pain, tenderness, weakness, or cramps (these could be signs of a rare but serious muscle problem); joint pain or swelling (this medicine can increase uric acid and may trigger gout); signs of a tendon problem such as pain, swelling, or difficulty moving a joint; upper stomach pain, dark urine, or yellowing of your skin or eyes (possible liver problems); or an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, or trouble breathing. Also call your doctor if you become pregnant or plan to become pregnant.
when_it_works: This medicine starts working right away, but it usually takes about 4 to 8 weeks before you and your doctor can see the full effect on your cholesterol levels through a blood test. Even if you feel fine, keep taking it every day as directed. Cholesterol usually causes no symptoms, so you may not feel any different — but the medicine is still protecting your heart and blood vessels.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Do not use this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, as it may harm the unborn baby. Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine. Talk to your doctor about safe birth control options. Children: This medicine is not approved for use in children. Older adults: Older patients may use this medicine, but your doctor will monitor you closely for side effects such as muscle or joint problems. Kidney or liver disease: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver problems, as dose adjustments or closer monitoring may be needed.
